name: Law Codes (e.g., Hammurabi) and Treaties

objectives.text: Recall that God gave His people the Ten Commandments written on two tablets of stone
Name the Ten Commandments as the rules God gave His people at Mount Sinai
Recall that kings in Bible times, such as Hammurabi of Babylon, carved their laws on large stones for people to see
Explain why God reminded Israel that He had rescued them from Egypt before giving them His commandments
Summarize the rule of eye for eye as a command for judges to make a punishment fit the wrong rather than permission for personal revenge
Explain what an ancient treaty was as a formal agreement in which a great king and a lesser king or people made promises and accepted obligations
Compare the penalties for theft in Hammurabi's code with the restitution required in the law of Moses
Explain how the covenant at Sinai presents God as Israel's great King and Israel as His treasured people
Identify the main parts of a second millennium suzerain-vassal treaty, including preamble, historical prologue, stipulations, deposit and reading, witnesses, and blessings and curses
Analyze how the book of Deuteronomy follows the outline of an ancient suzerain-vassal treaty
Distinguish apodictic law from casuistic law by classifying examples from the Book of the Covenant
Connect the blessings and curses of the Mosaic covenant to the sanctions that closed ancient treaties
Explain why the tablets of the covenant and the Book of the Law were placed in or beside the ark in light of the ancient practice of depositing treaty copies in a sanctuary
Explain how the Mosaic law protected servants, sojourners, widows, and orphans in ways that differed from other ancient Near Eastern law codes
Compare how ancient Near Eastern law codes and the Torah treat the value of human life, using cases such as the goring ox and class-based penalties
Analyze how the prophets bring a covenant lawsuit against Israel by calling witnesses and charging the people with breaking the covenant
Evaluate the law of retaliation as a principle that limited vengeance and applied equal justice to native Israelite and sojourner alike
Analyze a Hittite vassal treaty in translation alongside the covenant renewal at Shechem to identify shared covenant elements and key differences
Explain how the Westminster Confession's distinction of moral, ceremonial, and judicial law applies to the case laws of Moses that resemble ancient Near Eastern codes
Write an argument showing how Israel's law, unlike royal law codes, is grounded in the holy character of God as its giver

changes: Replaced the generic K safety objective and grade 3 'observe' objective with on-topic competencies (stone tablets, the law's preface). Kept and reworded the Ten Commandments, Hammurabi stele, eye for eye, treaty definition, Hammurabi comparison, suzerain treaty, apodictic/casuistic, blessings/curses, protection of vulnerable, value of life, lex talionis, Hittite research, and grounding in God's character objectives, giving them specific texts. Narrowed the Hammurabi comparison to theft and restitution. Reframed 'God is our King' from personal application to explaining the Sinai covenant. Split treaty structure into identifying its parts and analyzing Deuteronomy. Added treaty deposit practice, the prophetic covenant lawsuit, and the Westminster threefold division of the law as it bears on case law. Avoided dating questions left to the chronology sibling.
